title: The Magnet Field Probe
summary: Probe the axial and equatorial field of a short bar magnet and find where it cancels an outside field.
subject: physics
concepts: Axial field of a short magnet
Equatorial field of a short magnet
Null point against an external field
learningOutcome: The student can find the axial and equatorial fields of a short bar magnet with their directions, use the inverse-cube dependence on distance, and find where the field cancels an external field.

levels.title: Axis and equator
levels.adds: Baseline: B(axis) = (μ₀/4π) 2m/r³ along m, and B(equator) = (μ₀/4π) m/r³ against m (Ex 5.7).
hints: μ₀/4π = 10⁻⁷ T m/A. Change r to metres.
On the axis the field is twice the equatorial value at the same distance.
The axial field points along m; the equatorial field points opposite to m.

levels.title: The null point
levels.adds: More steps: find where the field of the magnet on its axis cancels an opposing external field.
hints: Slide the probe and watch the net field change sign.
At the null point (μ₀/4π) 2m/r³ equals the external field.
Rearrange for r and take a cube root.

levels.title: Scale it
levels.adds: New idea: use the 1/r³ law and the factor of 2 to predict one field from another without knowing m (Section 5.2.4).
hints: The equatorial field at r is half the axial field at the same r.
Divide by k³ when the distance is multiplied by k.

misconceptions: The field of a bar magnet falls as 1/r², like a point charge
The axial and equatorial fields point the same way
The equatorial field is stronger than the axial field
